# Kammakathā (Kv 21.8)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kammakathā* is the eighth and concluding debate of the twenty-first chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 21.8), preserved within the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [von Hinüber 1994; SuttaCentral]. In the Pali Text Society edition, it begins at Kv 611, line 28 [von Hinüber 1994]. Doctrinally, the controversy investigates whether *kamma* (action) is *niyata* ("definite") or *aniyata* ("indefinite") [von Hinüber 1994]. This inquiry centers on the threefold classification of actions according to the timing of their results: *diṭṭhadhammavedanīya* (actions ripening in the present lifetime), *upapajjavedanīya* (actions ripening in the immediately following existence), and *aparāpariyavedanīya* (actions ripening in subsequent existences) [von Hinüber 1994]. The debate questions whether an action belonging to the first category is completely exhausted in the present life or can continue to produce consequences in future existences, with analogous questions raised for the other two classes [von Hinüber 1994].

SuttaCentral records canonical connections and mentions of related material in the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33, PTS DN iii 207), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2), the preceding *Dhammakathā* (Kv 21.7), and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 21) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies 119 matching Pali passages across twelve texts [DharmaNexus]. Its highest internal alignment is with the contiguous debate *Dhammakathā* (Kv 21.7, sharing segments §0.1–3.6), along with textual links to other *Kathāvatthu* chapters (Kv 21.4, Kv 9.7, Kv 18.9, Kv 16.7), the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1), the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3), the *Vicayahārasampāta* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 21), and post-canonical treatises and commentaries such as the *Visuddhimagga*, *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā*, and *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also finds cross-language matches in Tibetan versions of Abhidharmic commentaries, including the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā-lakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093-2) and the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā* (D4092-2) [DharmaNexus]. A modern translation is listed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
